slides.say: A motorbike travels nine kilometers in fifteen minutes. A train travels fifteen kilometers in nine minutes. What is the difference between their speeds, in kilometers per hour?
So they ask for speeds in kilometers per hour, but the times are in minutes. The units don't match.
We'll solve it in two different ways. Let's start with the math way. We turn the minutes into hours.
Let's start with the motorbike. Fifteen minutes is fifteen out of sixty, a quarter of an hour.
at: Fifteen minutes is fifteen out of sixty

slides.say: The speed is the distance divided by the time. Nine divided by a quarter is nine times four, thirty-six kilometers per hour.
Now the train. Nine minutes is nine sixtieths of an hour.
Fifteen divided by nine sixtieths is fifteen times sixty, over nine.
Fifteen times sixty is nine hundred, and nine hundred divided by nine is a hundred. So the train goes a hundred kilometers per hour.
They ask for the difference, so a hundred minus thirty-six. Before a long subtraction, here are two quick ways.
Here's the first way. We add four to both numbers, so the second one is a round forty. A hundred four minus forty is sixty-four.
Here's another way. We walk from thirty-six to a round forty, that's four. Then from forty to a hundred, that's sixty.
Four plus sixty is sixty-four. So the difference is sixty-four kilometers per hour.
A hundred thirty-six, choice number four, adds the speeds instead.
[pause] Now by understanding, with identical ratios. This way saves most of the work. We start again from the givens.
The motorbike goes nine kilometers in fifteen minutes. We want one hour, sixty minutes.
From fifteen to sixty is times four. So the distance is times four too. Nine times four is thirty-six kilometers in one hour.
The train goes fifteen kilometers in nine minutes. From nine to sixty isn't a whole step. So first we divide both by three. That's five kilometers every three minutes.
An hour is twenty times three minutes. So five times twenty, a hundred kilometers in one hour.
at: An hour is twenty times three
a hundred kilometers in one hour

slides.say: If you don't see that step, use the triangle value from topic twenty-two. Multiply along the diagonal, fifteen times sixty, and divide by what's left, nine. That's a hundred too.
A hundred minus thirty-six is sixty-four. The same answer.
at: A hundred minus thirty-six is sixty-four
